SAM instance segmentation of touching/overlapping triangular nanoparticles with per-object morphology

Interpretation

The analysis segments a field of touching/overlapping triangular gold nanoparticles imaged by TEM at a resolved pixel size of 0.355 nm/px. Of 31 detected objects, 28 fully-interior particles were quantified while 3 edge-truncated particles were (correctly) excluded from statistics. The extracted per-particle areas were converted to an 'equivalent edge length' assuming an equilateral triangle (A = (sqrt(3)/4)*L^2), which is the physically meaningful size metric for these plate-like triangular prisms grown by anisotropic (facet-selective) colloidal synthesis. The size distribution is tight and unimodal: median edge 100.4 nm, mean 100.9 nm, std 7.7 nm (CV ~7.7%), spanning ~89-128 nm. This narrow, single-peaked distribution is the key physical result: it indicates a highly monodisperse population, consistent with a well-controlled seed-mediated growth where all particles nucleated and grew under near-uniform conditions. Monodispersity of edge length is important because the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) of triangular Au nanoprisms is governed primarily by edge length and tip sharpness; a ~8% edge-length spread implies a correspondingly narrow, well-defined plasmonic response — desirable for sensing, SERS, and photothermal applications. The absence of a low-value fragment population (no cluster of areas below ~1/4 of the ~4360 nm^2 median, i.e. no spike near ~1000 nm^2) argues against over-segmentation: SAM split the touching triangles into physically plausible whole objects rather than shards. The one clear outlier at 7086 nm^2 (~128 nm 'edge') sits far from the main mode and is flagged as a probable merged mask of two overlapping triangles; treated as an artifact, the true upper tail is closer to ~112 nm. Conversely, the dense, very-dark cluster in the lower-center/left may harbor a few heavily overlapping prisms that were merged or under-detected, so the true count is slightly uncertain (likely within the recommended ~±20%). Net interpretation: a uniform, ~100 nm-edge triangular Au nanoprism ensemble with a small number of segmentation ambiguities confined to the most overlapped/darkest regions.

3. Scientific Claims

Claim 1: The triangular Au nanoprisms form a highly monodisperse population with a median equivalent edge length of 100.4 nm (mean 100.9 nm, std 7.7 nm, CV ~7.7%) and a unimodal size distribution (n=28 interior particles).

Scientific Impact: A ~8% edge-length dispersion indicates excellent synthetic control (uniform seed-mediated anisotropic growth) and predicts a narrow, well-defined LSPR, which is critical for reproducible plasmonic performance in SERS, biosensing, and photothermal applications where edge length sets the resonance wavelength.

Literature Search Query: Has anyone achieved seed-mediated synthesis of triangular Au nanoprisms with ~100 nm edge length and sub-10% edge-length dispersion, and correlated that monodispersity with LSPR linewidth?

Keywords: gold nanoprisms, monodispersity, edge length, LSPR, anisotropic growth, TEM morphometry

4. Caveats & Limitations

Edge length is derived from segmented area assuming an ideal equilateral triangle, so tip truncation/rounding and any prism thickness variation are not captured. The largest 'particle' (7086 nm^2, ~128 nm) is a probable merged mask of two overlapping triangles and should be excluded before reporting the size range; the very-dark, heavily overlapped cluster (lower-center/left) may contain merged or under-detected prisms, so the total count (31) carries ~±20% uncertainty and should be checked against visual inspection. Statistics reflect only the 28 interior particles; 3 edge-truncated objects were excluded. TEM projection cannot distinguish flat-lying prisms from any tilted/stacked ones, which could bias apparent area.
